newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products becalmed, prices stable.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products becalmed, prices stable.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady in slow, holiday-affected business, traders said.
Gas oil was inactive. Outright prices rose 75 cents a tonne in line with a rise in the futures market inspired by freezing temperatures across Europe.
"Physical's been dead today," a trader said.

Premiums for Russian continued at around cif high Med flat basis Genoa. Russians were available and traders said they expected increased buying interest for heating oil after the New Year holiday at the end of the week.
Low sulphur diesel interest is moribund apart from that for Algerian material. The Asian arb is closed.
Naphtha held steady in quiet trade.
Traders said that though the European market was looking fairly lengthy there was little downward pressure on prices with few sellers around.
They said some equity holders were looking to take product transatlantic, with better U.S. gasoline demand expected to provide some offtake for reforming naphtha.
Notional cargo offers held around $217-$218 a tonne cif Med with nearest bids around $4 lower.
Gasoline was steady to soft in thin trade with most first half January programs already completed and East Med demand thinning. Premium unleaded cargoes were valued around $221 a tonne cif Med.

High sulphur cracked fuel oil prices were notionally little changed from Monday, with prices around $107 fob Med. But offers were notional, with most players out of the market because of the public holiday.
Low sulphur markets were also becalmed and the main Italian buyer was not active -- in effect killing off any activity.
